newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady to lower, pork bellies higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady to lower, pork bellies higher.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent a lb lower while pork bellies were called 0.200 to 0.500 cent higher, analysts said.

Increasing hog movement as temperatures moderate in the western Corn Belt was expected to keep pressure on hog futures. Hogs backed up by the latest cold snap should come to market by the weekend, analysts said.

However, losses could be limited by the firmer tone to cash pork prices and higher pork cutout values Tuesday. Expectations of higher pork belly futures could also lend support in the hog pit, they said.

Pork belly futures were called higher following Tueday's bullishly-construed weekly CME Out-of-Town Storage Report. CME reported a net out movement of 194,000 lbs last week compared with the bulk of early estimates of unchanged to in 600,000 lbs. A firm tone to the cash belly market should also provide support, they said.
However, the outlook for larger hog kills going into the weekend may temper upside potential, analysts and traders said.
